references.text: The Lord's hand was against the Egyptians with a plague, showing the same expression 'the Lord's hand' as a sign of God's judgment and punishment.
Describes God's judgment on the unfaithful generation that was to die in the wilderness, which is the same event referred to in Deuteronomy 2:15.
The spies who brought back a bad report about the land died from a plague sent by the Lord, illustrating God's direct intervention against the disobedient.
The Lord's wrath against the generation that refused to enter the land, which led to their wandering in the wilderness until they died out.
God ended their days in futility and their years in terror, reflecting on that same period of wilderness wandering.
The Lord raised His hand against them to let them fall in the wilderness, a poetic restatement of the same event.
Hebrews refers to those who fell in the wilderness because of disobedience and warns against the same kind of unbelief.
Paul mentions that God was not pleased with most of them, and they were struck down in the wilderness as a warning to believers.
